meta.name: chopsticksAI
meta.tagline: The Chopsticks HQ assistant — live answers via chopstickshq.com, offline KB for product help.

intents.label: What is chopsticksAI?
intents.answer:
I'm cs.AI {{VERSION:chopsticks-ai}} (chopsticksAI) — the assistant built by Chopsticks HQ.

Ask me anything: general knowledge, code, writing, or anything about the Chopsticks apps. Product answers come from a maintained knowledge base, so version numbers and install commands are the real ones.

Available on macOS, in your browser, and in Terminal (csai). No API key on your side. In live mode your question is sent to chopstickshq.com (then a language model) to answer; we don't keep a chat history or analytics on what you ask. Details: chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/privacy.html

intents.label: What can you help with?
intents.answer:
I can answer general questions — coding, writing, science, recommendations, casual chat — and I'm also the in-house expert on Chopsticks HQ software:

• rNitro — install, features, troubleshooting, CLI, Linux, Windows, Homebrew
• Fathom Air — battery monitor, install, uninstall
• Fathom Pro — weather, AI chat, unlock keys
• Chopsticks HQ — macOS catalog app
• cs.AI / chopsticksAI — macOS Agents app, web app, Terminal CLI (csai), and Lab
• ARENA — the FPS game
• Guides, privacy, licensing, and downloads

Offline fallback covers Chopsticks HQ topics only. Just ask in plain English.

intents.label: How does chopsticksAI work?
phrases: do you use a cloud model
intents.answer:
chopsticksAI answers in two layers:

1. Live answers — your question goes to chopstickshq.com/api/chopsticks-ai, which matches facts from a keyword-scored knowledge base (not vector embeddings), optionally runs Chromium web search (Google + DuckDuckGo), then calls a language model. No account and no API key on your side.

2. Offline fallback — if the endpoint is unreachable, on cooldown, or errors out, chopsticksAI answers from the compiled knowledge base on your device for Chopsticks HQ topics.

There is no embedding index or semantic vector store. Inside rNitro's Chat tab, chopsticksAI is the default provider and works the same way.

intents.label: Do you send my questions anywhere?
intents.answer:
Live mode: your question goes to chopstickshq.com/api/chopsticks-ai, which may call a language-model provider to draft the reply. Chopsticks HQ does not create an account for you, does not require your own API key, and does not keep a searchable log or analytics of what you ask.

Offline fallback: if the API is down or on cooldown, ChopsticksAI answers from the on-device knowledge base for Chopsticks HQ topics only — nothing leaves your device in that path.

rNitro and Fathom themselves send no usage telemetry. Full note: chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/privacy.html

intents.label: What are the current app versions?
How do I install the ChopsticksAI macOS app?
intents.answer:
ChopsticksAI for macOS is free (currently {{VERSION:chopsticks-ai}}).

1. Download the App ZIP from chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/
2. Or run: curl -fsSL https://chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/install-chopsticks-ai.sh | bash
3. It installs to ~/Applications/chopsticksAI.app

The Agents Window includes a Chromium browser rail whose home page is chopstickshq.com. Live chat uses chopstickshq.com — no API key from you. If the network is down, product questions fall back to the on-device knowledge base.

intents.label: macOS says ChopsticksAI can't be opened
intents.answer:
That's Gatekeeper on an unsigned download — not malware.

Fix:
1. Right-click chopsticksAI.app → Open → Open
2. Or clear quarantine: xattr -cr ~/Applications/chopsticksAI.app
3. Re-run the Terminal installer if needed

The install script already clears quarantine for ~/Applications installs.

intents.label: What is the cs.AI web app or Lab?
intents.answer:
cs.AI runs in the browser two ways:

• Main web app — chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/web/ (Cursor-style Agents UI, Chromium browser rail, attachments, account sync)
• Legacy Lab — chopstickshq.com/chopailab/ (full-page agent with effort tiers and file export)

The sidebar widget on other HQ pages is the lighter chat. All use the same live model and allowance as macOS.

intents.label: Is there a Terminal CLI for cs.AI?
intents.answer:
Yes — the cs.AI Terminal CLI (command: csai) is a full-screen terminal agent.

Install:
curl -fsSL https://chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/install-csai-cli.sh | bash

Then run csai for the interactive UI, or csai ask "question" for one-shot answers. Same live model and allowance as macOS and web. Update with csai update.

intents.label: What is the Chromium browser in cs.AI?
intents.answer:
cs.AI {{VERSION:chopsticks-ai}} includes a Chromium-style browser in the macOS Agents Window and the web app.

• Home page: chopstickshq.com
• Address bar accepts URLs or Google search queries
• Standalone search on chopstickshq.com/chopsticks-ai/#search uses the same Chromium engine (Google + DuckDuckGo)
• Queries mentioning chopsticks always prioritize chopstickshq.com in search results

intents.label: What is the Chopsticks HQ macOS app?
intents.answer:
Chopsticks HQ is a free macOS catalog app (currently {{VERSION:chopsticks-hq}}) that lists Chopsticks products and opens their pages.

Install from chopstickshq.com or the downloads on the HQ site. It uses a WebView for product pages and links into ChopsticksAI Lab — it is not a separate AI model.

intents.label: What is Chopsticks HQ?
intents.answer:
Chopsticks HQ is the home for a small set of macOS apps and side projects, made by chopsticks.

Main apps:
• rNitro — menu bar system monitor
• Fathom Air — battery monitor
• Fathom Pro — battery + weather + AI
• ARENA — an FPS game

Everything is free, with no accounts and no telemetry.

intents.label: Where are the guides?
intents.answer:
Guides live at chopstickshq.com/guides/

Current topics:
• Free Mac menu bar monitor
• rNitro battery readings on Apple Silicon
• Minecraft gens Skript checklist

The index always lists what's there — more get added as they are written.

intents.label: What apps are there?
intents.answer:
The Chopsticks HQ lineup:

• rNitro — CPU, temperature, RAM, GPU, battery and network in your menu bar
• Fathom Air — battery drain and power draw, local only
• Fathom Pro — Fathom Air plus local weather and AI chat
• ARENA — a procedurally generated FPS for macOS
• Chopsticks Shaders — an Iris shader pack for Minecraft

All free.

intents.label: Is it free?
intents.answer:
Yes — everything on Chopsticks HQ is free.

No subscriptions, no trials, no ads, no in-app purchases. Fathom Pro needs an unlock key, but those are free too (see the vault).

If an app asks you for money, it isn't ours.

For bugs in rNitro specifically, opening a GitHub issue is faster:

intents.label: Where are the terms and privacy policy?
intents.answer:
Each product has its own terms:

intents.label: What is rNitro?
intents.answer:
rNitro is a free, open-source system monitor that lives in your Mac's menu bar.

It shows live CPU usage, temperature, memory, GPU, battery, and network — plus per-core breakdowns, a built-in benchmark, a game overlay, and an optional Bitcoin price readout.

Free, no account, no telemetry. macOS 14+ (Sonoma or later).

intents.label: How do I install rNitro on macOS?
intents.answer:
The Terminal install is the recommended path — it installs to ~/Applications and clears the quarantine flag, so Gatekeeper never blocks it.

Copy the Terminal command from chopstickshq.com/rnitro and paste it into Terminal.

The App ZIP is a fallback. Because browser downloads get macOS's quarantine flag, Gatekeeper will block it on first launch — right-click the app, choose Open, then Open again.

intents.label: Install rNitro with Homebrew
intents.answer:
If you use Homebrew:

brew tap ilikemacos/rnitro
brew install rnitro

That installs the stable formula. For the latest experimental build with the full feature set, use the Terminal installer from chopstickshq.com/rnitro instead.

No Homebrew? The curl one-liner on the rNitro page works without it.

intents.label: macOS says the app can't be opened
intents.answer:
That's macOS quarantining anything downloaded through a browser — normal for indie apps.

Don't click Move to Trash. Either:

1. Right-click the app → Open → Open again, or
2. System Settings → Privacy & Security → press Open at the bottom, or
3. In Terminal: xattr -cr ~/Applications/rNitro.app

The Terminal installer avoids this entirely — it clears the flag for you.

intents.label: How do I uninstall rNitro?
intents.answer:
macOS: quit rNitro from the menu bar, then delete rNitro.app from ~/Applications (or /Applications).

To remove settings too:
defaults delete com.chopsticks.rnitro

Linux: rm -rf ~/.local/share/rnitro ~/.local/bin/rnitro ~/.local/share/applications/rnitro.desktop

Windows: right-click the tray icon → Exit, then delete the folder you unzipped.

intents.label: How do updates work?
intents.answer:
rNitro checks for updates when it launches and can fetch the latest build in-app.

You can also just re-run the Terminal install command — it always resolves whatever version.json lists as current, so it upgrades you in place.

Old releases are kept on the Archives page.

intents.label: What version is current?
intents.answer:
The current macOS build is v1.4.0-Final.

Other platforms:
• CLI — v0.2-cli
• Linux — v0.1 Beta pre-release
• Windows — v6.0.2 (deprecated)

The live numbers always come from chopstickshq.com/rnitro/version.json.

intents.label: What are the system requirements?
phrases: will it run on my mac
intents.answer:
rNitro needs macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later.

It uses SwiftUI APIs introduced in macOS 14, so Big Sur, Monterey, and Ventura can't run the current build. There's an info pack on the site describing the older-macOS situation.

Apple Silicon is the primary target; Intel builds exist but stopped receiving updates after v1.2.5-Beta.

intents.label: Does it work on Intel Macs?
intents.answer:
Intel Macs are no longer receiving updates. The last Intel build is v1.2.5-Beta, still downloadable from the Intel Mac tab on the rNitro page.

Apple Silicon (M1 and newer) gets all current development.

intents.label: How accurate is the temperature?
phrases: where does the temperature come from
intents.answer:
rNitro reads real sensor data from your Mac's SMC — the same controller iStat Menus, TG Pro, and Macs Fan Control use.

If the SMC can't be reached or your chip's sensor keys aren't recognised, it falls back to macOS's own thermal state (Nominal / Fair / Serious / Critical), smoothed using live CPU load so the gauge never goes blank.

These are informational readings, not a substitute for hardware diagnostics.

intents.label: What CPU information does it show?
intents.answer:
rNitro shows total CPU load with a 60-second history graph, colour-coded by intensity, plus:

• Per-core usage bars and clock speeds for every logical core
• Base and boost clock estimates
• Package power draw in watts
• Load average

Open the Monitor tab and click any stat for a detail view.

intents.label: Does it monitor RAM?
intents.answer:
Yes — used vs total memory in GB, a percentage, and macOS memory pressure.

The Advisor tab will tell you whether your current usage is above the RAM threshold you've set, and suggest checking Activity Monitor when it is.

intents.label: Does it monitor the GPU?
intents.answer:
Yes — GPU utilisation as a percentage, with its own alert threshold.

High GPU usage during games, video export, or Metal work is normal; the Advisor tab flags it only when it crosses the limit you set.

intents.label: What battery info does rNitro show?
intents.answer:
rNitro shows battery percentage, whether you're on AC or battery, charging state, and a low-battery alert at a threshold you choose.

For deeper battery work — power draw in watts, per-process energy attribution, and drain explanations — Fathom Air is the dedicated tool, and it's also free.

intents.label: Does it show network speed?
intents.answer:
Yes — live download and upload throughput in Mbps, sampled continuously.

It measures throughput on your active interface; it isn't a speed test, so numbers reflect what your Mac is actually transferring right now.

intents.label: Is there a benchmark?
intents.answer:
Yes — a Cinebench-style benchmark built into the popover, giving single-core and multi-core scores from a fixed, repeatable render workload.

There's also a stress test for pushing the CPU deliberately. Both will heat your Mac up; that's expected.

intents.label: What is the game overlay / FPS HUD?
intents.answer:
Press ⌥⇧O to toggle an overlay showing CPU%, GPU%, temperature and RAM on top of fullscreen games.

For true frame rates, use "Launch App with FPS HUD" from the right-click menu — that enables Apple's native Metal performance HUD for that game.

intents.label: Why is there a Bitcoin price?
intents.answer:
It's an optional menu bar extra — live BTC/USD refreshed every 30 seconds from CoinGecko's public API. No API key, and you can turn it off in Settings.

It's the one feature that makes a network request; everything else is local.

intents.label: What are the tabs in the app?
intents.answer:
Click the menu bar icon to open the popover:

• Monitor — live stats and detail views
• Advisor — asks about YOUR Mac using live readings, sets alert thresholds
• Chat — AI chat, including chopsticksAI and bring-your-own-key providers
• Cleaner — reclaim disk space
• Lab — experimental toys (Beta builds)
• Settings — appearance, menu bar items, alerts

intents.label: What is the Advisor tab?
intents.answer:
The Advisor is a built-in assistant that reads your live CPU, temperature, RAM, GPU, battery, disk and network — no API key needed.

Ask it things like "my specs" or "is my temp ok?". Tap ⚙ to set custom warning thresholds, and it will post proactive alerts in the chat when values cross them.

It answers about your hardware; chopsticksAI answers about the apps themselves.

intents.label: How do I set alerts and thresholds?
intents.answer:
Advisor tab → ⚙. You can set:

• Temperature warning and critical levels
• CPU, RAM, and GPU percentage limits
• Low-battery percentage
• Proactive alerts on or off
• macOS notification banners for critical temperatures

Alerts have a 90-second cooldown per type so they don't spam you.

intents.label: What AI providers does rNitro support?
phrases: can i use my own api key
intents.answer:
The Chat tab supports chopsticksAI (built in, no key), plus bring-your-own-key providers:

• Cloud — Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, Grok, DeepSeek, OpenRouter
• Local — LM Studio, Ollama, Hermes (no key, runs on your machine)

Cloud keys are AES-256 encrypted in your Keychain and only ever sent to that provider.

intents.label: Is rNitro safe to run?
intents.answer:
The installers verify their own SHA-256 checksum before running, and refuse to continue if it doesn't match.

The full app source is included inline in the shell installers, so you can read everything before executing. rNitro is also on GitHub.

No telemetry, no account, no data collection.

intents.label: Is there a command line version?
intents.answer:
Yes — rNitro CLI (v0.2-cli), a btop-style terminal dashboard for when you're on SSH or don't want a menu bar app.

It shows CPU, memory, disk I/O, network, battery, and top processes. Keys: q quits, r refreshes. Use rnitro --once for one-shot JSON output.

Runs on macOS and Linux, Python 3, no GUI required.

intents.label: Is there a Linux version?
intents.answer:
There's a Linux pre-release: v0.1-Linux-Beta-Pre-release-x64.

It's a GTK 4 + libadwaita desktop app needing Python 3.10+. Download the tarball or install-rNitro-linux.sh from the Linux page and run:
bash install-rNitro-linux.sh

It installs to ~/.local/share/rnitro. Apple-only sensors (SMC, Low Power Mode) show as N/A.

intents.label: Is there a Windows version?
intents.answer:
Windows is no longer actively developed, but the last build stays available: v6.0.2-Windows-x64, shipped as a portable ZIP.

Unzip it anywhere and run rNitro.exe — it lives in the system tray. Needs 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and the .NET 8 Desktop Runtime. Windows 8.1 and earlier aren't supported.

Run as administrator if you want CPU temperatures; Windows hides thermal sensors from unelevated apps.

intents.label: Where are older versions?
intents.answer:
The Archives page lists every hosted macOS DMG: chopstickshq.com/rnitro/archives.html

Older PKG, ZIP and shell installers are also still hosted, and GitHub Releases keeps a full history.

intents.label: What is Fathom Air?
intents.answer:
Fathom Air is a free macOS menu bar app focused entirely on battery and power.

It shows charge percentage, time remaining, package watts, power distribution, which apps are draining you, and an experimental charge limit — all read locally from your Mac.

No accounts, no telemetry, no AI. macOS 14+.

intents.label: How do I install Fathom Air?
intents.answer:
Use the curl installer from chopstickshq.com/fathom — it resolves the current version, verifies the download's SHA-256, and installs to ~/Applications without tripping Gatekeeper:

curl -fsSL https://chopstickshq.com/fathom/install-fathom.sh | bash

The App ZIP is a fallback, but Gatekeeper will block it on first launch (right-click → Open, then Open again).

intents.label: What version is Fathom Air?
intents.answer:
Fathom Air is on v0.3.8-Beta.

The installer always resolves whatever chopstickshq.com/fathom/version.json lists, so re-running it upgrades you.

intents.label: How do I uninstall Fathom Air?
intents.answer:
Quit Fathom Air from the menu bar, then delete Fathom Air.app from ~/Applications (or /Applications).

To remove saved settings:
defaults delete com.chopstickshq.fathom

intents.label: What's the difference between Fathom and rNitro?
intents.answer:
They overlap a little but aim at different things:

• rNitro — the whole system: CPU, temperature, GPU, RAM, network, benchmarks, game overlay
• Fathom Air — battery and power specifically: watts, per-process energy, drain attribution, charge limits

Many people run both. Both are free.

intents.label: How accurate are Fathom's battery numbers?
intents.answer:
Charge percentage aims to match the macOS menu bar exactly.

Remaining time, wattage, power distribution and per-process attribution are estimates derived from system APIs — they vary with workload and can be briefly wrong after you plug or unplug.

They're informational, not a substitute for manufacturer diagnostics.

intents.label: What is Fathom Pro?
intents.answer:
Fathom Pro is Fathom Air plus two things:

• Local weather — from Open-Meteo using your Mac's location; the menu bar can show % and °C together
• AI chat and Explain drain — using your own OpenRouter, Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic key

It's also a regular Cmd+Tab app with a full window. Free, unlocked with a key.

intents.label: How do I unlock Fathom Pro?
phrases: where do i get a key
intents.answer:
You need an oi-pl key. It's free and there are two ways to get one:

1. The vault at chopstickshq.com/vault/ — a password-gated generator; each Generate mints a new random key
2. The homepage scavenger hunt — on the "Small lab." headline, click the first L after the A in "Small"

Then paste it into Fathom Pro → Activate.

An oi-pl key is a client-side unlock token only — not an OpenAI or OpenRouter API key, and it carries no credit.

intents.label: Do I need my own AI keys for Fathom Pro?
phrases: do i need an api key
do i need my own api key
intents.answer:
Yes — Fathom Pro's AI features need your own API key from a supported provider (OpenRouter, Gemini, OpenAI, or Anthropic).

Keys are stored in your macOS Keychain and are never sent to us. You contract directly with that provider and pay their charges; we receive nothing and have no control over their pricing or availability.

Add them under Customize → AI → API Config.

intents.label: What data does Fathom Pro send out?
phrases: what gets sent to the ai
intents.answer:
Two things leave your Mac, both only when you use those features:

• Weather — approximate location coordinates go to Open-Meteo to fetch a forecast
• AI chat / Explain drain — your message plus a battery and system snapshot go to whichever provider you configured

Nothing goes to Chopsticks HQ. Don't use the AI features with anything you wouldn't share with that provider.

intents.label: What is Explain drain?
intents.answer:
Explain drain sends a live snapshot of your battery and power state to your configured AI provider and asks it to explain what's using the most energy.

Because it's generated by a language model it can be wrong or misattribute usage — treat it as a hint, not a diagnosis. The raw per-process energy numbers in the app are the reliable part.

intents.label: How does the weather feature work?
intents.answer:
Fathom Pro asks Open-Meteo for a forecast based on your Mac's approximate location, and can display the outside temperature next to your battery percentage in the menu bar.

It's third-party data with no guarantee of accuracy or availability, and it isn't suitable for navigation or any safety-critical use.

intents.label: What is ARENA?
intents.answer:
ARENA is a first-person shooter for macOS, written in C++17 with OpenGL 4.1.

Every run generates a fresh 5 km × 5 km world from a compact seed using spectral synthesis — the terrain is a summed waveform turned into a heightmap — then populates it with buildings, structures, and movable furniture.

Free, from chopstickshq.com/arena-fps/.

intents.label: How do I install ARENA?
intents.answer:
Download ARENA-macOS.zip from chopstickshq.com/arena-fps/, unzip it, and drag ARENA.app to Applications.

Gatekeeper will block it on first launch since it's downloaded through a browser — right-click → Open, then Open again, or run:
xattr -cr /Applications/ARENA.app

intents.label: Where does ARENA save progress?
intents.answer:
ARENA saves to ~/Library/Application Support/ARENA/ — macOS's equivalent of AppData.

save.cfg holds your run: wave, kills, credits, weapons, position, world seed, and any furniture you've moved to build a base. settings.cfg holds graphics options.

Note that dying deletes the save — bases don't outlive a run.

intents.label: What are the controls?
intents.answer:
WASD to move, mouse to look, Space to jump, Shift to sprint.

Number keys switch weapons, R reloads, E interacts with and picks up furniture. Escape opens the menu.

From the title screen, W/A/S/D or Space starts the game.

intents.label: ARENA runs slowly
intents.answer:
Drop the graphics preset — Escape → Settings. MEDIUM is the default and targets a good balance; LOW disables terrain detail and shadows for much higher frame rates.

Make sure only one copy is running: two instances competing for the GPU is a common cause of sudden slowness.

intents.label: Can I build a base in ARENA?
intents.answer:
Yes — furniture is scattered around the world and can be picked up and repositioned with E to barricade a spot.

What you build persists across launches: the save records both the pieces and which chunks you've already explored, so returning to an area won't respawn a duplicate set on top of yours.

intents.label: What are Chopsticks Shaders?
intents.answer:
Chopsticks Shaders is an Iris shader pack for Minecraft, with volumetric lighting derived from Noble.

It's licensed GPL-3.0 because of that lineage. Available from chopstickshq.com/shaders/.

intents.label: What is the Minecraft portfolio?
intents.answer:
chopstickshq.com/minecraft/ is a portfolio of Minecraft server development work — custom systems, mechanics, and Skript development across a number of servers.

It's separate from the desktop apps.

intents.label: What is the vault?
intents.answer:
The vault at chopstickshq.com/vault/ is a password-gated generator for Fathom Pro unlock keys.

Each Generate mints a new random oi-pl key entirely in your browser. These are unlock tokens for Fathom Pro only — they are not cloud API keys and carry no credit.

intents.label: The app won't launch
intents.answer:
Try in this order:

1. If macOS blocked it, right-click → Open → Open again
2. Clear the quarantine flag: xattr -cr ~/Applications/rNitro.app
3. Confirm you're on macOS 14 or later — older versions can't run the current build
4. Re-run the Terminal installer to get a clean copy

Still stuck? Open an issue at github.com/ilikemacos/rNitro/issues/new with your macOS version and Mac model.

intents.label: Temperature shows N/A or looks wrong
intents.answer:
If the SMC sensor keys for your chip aren't recognised, rNitro falls back to macOS's thermal state and interpolates from CPU load — so the number stays plausible but isn't a direct reading.

On Windows, temperatures need administrator rights; Windows hides thermal sensors from unelevated processes.

On Linux, Apple-only sensors always show N/A.

intents.label: The app itself is using CPU
phrases: high cpu usage from the app
intents.answer:
rNitro is native Swift, not Electron — the app bundle is around 3.5 MB and idles low.

If it's using more than you'd expect, lower the refresh rate in Settings, turn off the Bitcoin ticker, and close the popover when you're not reading it — the live panel refreshes several times a second while open.

intents.label: The installer says checksum mismatch
intents.answer:
That's the installer protecting you — it downloaded a file whose SHA-256 doesn't match what version.json publishes, so it refused to install.

Usually it's a truncated or cached download. Try again; if it keeps failing, the mirror you hit may be stale. Report it at github.com/ilikemacos/rNitro/issues/new and include both hashes it printed.

intents.label: The download won't start
intents.answer:
Every download shows a terms dialog first — you have to press "I Agree & download" for the file to start.

If nothing happens after that, try the Terminal install instead, or grab the file straight from GitHub Releases.
